Download gridded population counts from WorldPop

Source: R/worldpop.R
get_worldpop.Rd

Finds and downloads WorldPop population counts for a country and year, for the whole population or for chosen age groups and sexes, and returns them as a single raster of people per cell.

Usage

get_worldpop(
  country,
  year,
  ages = NULL,
  sex = c("both", "female", "male"),
  resolution = c("100m", "1km"),
  constrained = FALSE,
  un_adjusted = FALSE,
  dest_dir = tempdir(),
  messages = getOption("RiskMap.messages", TRUE)
)

Arguments

country

ISO3 code of the country, for example "LBR" for Liberia.

year

Year of the population estimates.

ages

NULL (the default) for the whole population, or a vector c(from, to) of ages in years, for example c(20, Inf) for adults aged 20 and over or c(0, 4) for children under five. Both ends must match the WorldPop age groups (0, 1 to 4, 5 to 9, and so on in five-year groups, with an open-ended oldest group).

sex

"both" (the default), "female" or "male". Only used with ages.

resolution

"100m" (the default) or "1km".

constrained

Logical. FALSE (the default) uses the unconstrained estimates, which spread people over all land; TRUE uses the constrained estimates, which place people only in mapped settlements. See Details.

un_adjusted

Logical. If TRUE, national totals are adjusted to match United Nations population estimates. Available for the whole population of the unconstrained 2000 to 2020 estimates.

dest_dir

Directory for the downloaded files. Files already there are not downloaded again. Defaults to a temporary directory.

messages

Logical. Report the product and the number of files. Defaults to the option RiskMap.messages, or TRUE if it is not set.

Value

A SpatRaster with one layer, population, giving the number of people per cell.

Details

WorldPop distributes census-based population totals over a fine grid with statistical models that use covariates such as settlement maps, roads and night-time lights. The products differ in how people are placed:

  • Unconstrained estimates (constrained = FALSE) place people in every land cell, so sparsely populated or uninhabited areas receive small counts. They are available for every year from 2000 to 2020, at 100 m and 1 km, for the whole population and by age and sex. They suit population weights on grids of a few kilometres and analyses of past surveys.

  • Constrained estimates (constrained = TRUE) place people only in cells mapped as built-up settlements. They describe where people live more sharply, particularly at fine resolution, but can miss small rural settlements. This function uses the WorldPop release covering 2015 to 2030.

WorldPop also produces bottom-up estimates from microcensus surveys for a few countries, which this function does not cover.

The function queries the WorldPop catalogue at https://hub.worldpop.org/rest/data. The 1 km age and sex layers of the 2000 to 2020 release are not listed in the catalogue, and their addresses are built from WorldPop's naming pattern. When ages covers several age groups or both sexes, their counts are added together.

The result is in longitude and latitude. To aggregate the counts to the cells of a prediction grid, project them with terra::project() and method = "sum", sum them into larger cells with terra::aggregate(), and pass the result to create_grid() as raster.

References

WorldPop (www.worldpop.org). Please cite the WorldPop products used, as listed on the WorldPop website.

See also

create_grid()

Examples

# \donttest{
# Adults aged 20 and over in Liberia in 2011, at 1 km
adults <- get_worldpop("LBR", year = 2011, ages = c(20, Inf),
                       resolution = "1km")
#> ℹ WorldPop unconstrained 2000-2020 estimates at 1km, LBR 2011, aged 20 and
#>   over, in 26 files.
terra::global(adults, "sum", na.rm = TRUE)
#>                sum
#> population 1739127
# }
